title: Morris Water Maze: Spatial Learning and Memory Assessment in Mice
author: Sarah van Veen

steps.title: Perform Daily Training Trials
steps.instruction: Conduct daily training trials to assess spatial learning, using randomized starting positions to prevent position-based strategies.

substeps.instruction: Release each mouse from 4 different randomized starting positions (N, S, E, W quadrant edges).
Allow up to 100 s for the mouse to locate the hidden platform.
Allow the mouse to remain on the platform for 15 s once located.
If the platform is not located within 100 s, guide the mouse to the platform and allow 15 s there.
Return the mouse to a holding cage with dry bedding for 15–30 min between trials.

steps.title: Conduct Weekly Probe Trials
steps.instruction: Perform probe trials at the end of each working week to assess spatial memory consolidation.

substeps.instruction: Remove the hidden platform from the maze.
Release the mouse from the quadrant opposite to the target.
Record the search pattern using EthoVision.

steps.title: Adapt for Working Memory Version
steps.instruction: Modify the protocol for working memory assessment by repositioning the hidden platform to a new fixed location at the start of each day, maintaining the same daily trial structure.

steps.title: Analyze Behavioral Data
steps.instruction: Use EthoVision to compute variables and apply statistical tests to evaluate learning and memory.

substeps.instruction: Compute path length (cm), swim velocity (cm/s), and time spent in each zone/quadrant.
Analyze escape latency and path length across training days to determine the learning curve.
Compare time spent in the target quadrant versus other quadrants for probe trials.
Evaluate WT mice for progressive reduction in escape latency and target quadrant preference (>25% time), and KO mice for elevated escape latency or absence of quadrant preference.
